old: It once named the slant a weighted ball takes as it curves off a straight path.
Its journey ran from a slanted line, through a game of bowls, to a slant of the mind.
It may descend from a Vulgar Latin word meaning 'with two axes,' via Occitan and French.
clues: A name for a tendency of the mind, it first meant a literal slanted line, then the lopsided weighting that makes a ball curve in the game of bowls.
It's an inclination that tilts judgment unfairly toward or against something, subtler and more everyday than outright prejudice, as when a referee seems to favor the home team.
Psychologists warn about the confirmation kind, news outlets are accused of a media one, and dressmakers cut fabric on it, diagonally across the grain.
